title: Inguinal hernia surgery for children
what: The surgeon closes the opening in the groin where the hernia comes through. It is done under general anesthesia.
why: An inguinal hernia in children does not go away on its own. Surgery is done so it does not get trapped.
duration: surgery usually takes 20 to 40 minutes; you often go home the same day or the next
tell_doctor: If your child was born early
A cold, cough, or fever in the past 2 weeks
Any problems with anesthesia in the family

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, and sometimes a GP checkup. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Anesthetist
prepare.text: Before surgery, a pediatric anesthetist will talk with you. Tell them about your child's health.

prepare.title: Food and water
prepare.text: The clinic sets strict times for no food, formula, breast milk, and water. They are shorter for babies.

prepare.title: Talk to your child
prepare.text: Say calmly and honestly that they will have a sleep, and then it will hurt a little. Bring a favorite toy.

steps: Your child changes, and numbing cream may be put on the hand
In the operating room, your child falls asleep with a mask or an IV
The surgeon makes a small cut in the groin or works through small openings
The hernia sac is removed, and the opening is closed
The wound is taped or stitched
Your child wakes up, and you are called in
feel: After anesthesia, your child may be fussy and sleepy
The wound hurts for 1 to 3 days. You will get children's painkillers
Sometimes mild swelling in the groin or scrotum. It passes
after: Your child can usually drink and eat after a few hours
Active play, running, and cycling after 1 to 2 weeks, as the surgeon says
Keep the wound dry until you are told it is OK
Back to nursery or school usually after a few days
red_flags: A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or redness and pus from the wound
Severe pain, crying, or growing swelling in the groin or scrotum
Vomiting, or your child is very floppy: call emergency services

faq.q: Can we wait with the surgery?
faq.a: Surgery is usually planned without a long wait. If the hernia will not go back in and hurts, see a doctor right away.

faq.q: Is anesthesia dangerous for a child?
faq.a: Modern pediatric anesthesia is safe. The anesthetist will tailor it to your child's weight and health.

reminders.text: Your child's surgery is tomorrow. Food, milk, and water strictly until the time the clinic gave you. Bring a favorite toy.
